cards.front: classification
cards.back: Sorting living things into groups using their features.
cards.say: classification. Sorting living things into groups using their features.

cards.front: Why do scientists classify living things?
cards.back: It makes it easier to identify them and to understand how they are related.
cards.say: Why do scientists classify living things? It makes it easier to identify them and to understand how they are related.

cards.front: Name the main groups of living things.
cards.back: Animals, plants, fungi and microorganisms.
cards.say: Name the main groups of living things. Animals, plants, fungi and microorganisms.

cards.front: species
cards.back: A group of living things that are very alike and can have young together.
cards.say: species. A group of living things that are very alike and can have young together.

cards.front: vertebrates
cards.back: Animals with backbones: mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and fish.
cards.say: vertebrates. Animals with backbones: mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and fish.

cards.front: invertebrates
cards.back: Animals without backbones, such as insects, spiders, snails and worms.
cards.say: invertebrates. Animals without backbones, such as insects, spiders, snails and worms.

cards.front: fungi
cards.back: A group of living things that are not plants or animals. Mushrooms and moulds are fungi.
cards.say: fungi. A group of living things that are not plants or animals. Mushrooms and moulds are fungi.

cards.front: bacteria
cards.back: Microorganisms made of one tiny cell. Some cause disease, but many are useful.
cards.say: bacteria. Microorganisms made of one tiny cell. Some cause disease, but many are useful.

cards.front: branching key
cards.back: A diagram of yes or no questions that leads you to the name of a living thing.
cards.say: branching key. A diagram of yes or no questions that leads you to the name of a living thing.

cards.front: How is a branching key used?
cards.back: Start at the top. Answer each yes or no question about the living thing and follow the branch until you reach a name.
cards.say: How is a branching key used? Start at the top. Answer each yes or no question about the living thing and follow the branch until you reach a name.

cards.front: What makes a good key question?
cards.back: It can be answered with yes or no, and it is about a feature you can see, such as "Does it have six legs?"
cards.say: What makes a good key question? It can be answered with yes or no, and it is about a feature you can see, such as "Does it have six legs?"

cards.front: Why are questions like "Is it nice?" poor for a key?
cards.back: They are opinions, not features that everyone can check in the same way.
cards.say: Why are questions like "Is it nice?" poor for a key? They are opinions, not features that everyone can check in the same way.

cards.front: Which feature separates mammals from birds?
cards.back: Mammals have hair or fur. Birds have feathers.
cards.say: Which feature separates mammals from birds? Mammals have hair or fur. Birds have feathers.

cards.front: Which feature separates insects from spiders?
cards.back: Insects have six legs. Spiders have eight legs.
cards.say: Which feature separates insects from spiders? Insects have six legs. Spiders have eight legs.

cards.front: Which feature separates flowering plants from ferns?
cards.back: Flowering plants make flowers and seeds. Ferns make spores.
cards.say: Which feature separates flowering plants from ferns? Flowering plants make flowers and seeds. Ferns make spores.

cards.front: What does a key question about "wings" help to sort?
cards.back: Animals with wings, such as birds, bats and insects, from those without.
cards.say: What does a key question about "wings" help to sort? Animals with wings, such as birds, bats and insects, from those without.

cards.front: How do you build your own key?
cards.back: Choose a feature that splits the group in two, then keep splitting each group with a new yes or no question until each has a single member.
cards.say: How do you build your own key? Choose a feature that splits the group in two, then keep splitting each group with a new yes or no question until each has a single member.

cards.front: Why should each key question split the group?
cards.back: So that each answer takes you closer to a single name.
cards.say: Why should each key question split the group? So that each answer takes you closer to a single name.

cards.front: scientific name
cards.back: The two part name of a species in Latin that scientists everywhere use. Humans are Homo sapiens.
cards.say: scientific name. The two part name of a species in Latin that scientists everywhere use. Humans are Homo sapiens.

cards.front: Why do scientists use scientific names?
cards.back: People in different countries use different common names, but the scientific name is the same everywhere.
cards.say: Why do scientists use scientific names? People in different countries use different common names, but the scientific name is the same everywhere.

cards.front: microorganism
cards.back: A living thing so small that you need a microscope to see it.
cards.say: microorganism. A living thing so small that you need a microscope to see it.

cards.front: Give one feature of all animals.
cards.back: They cannot make their own food, so they eat other living things.
cards.say: Give one feature of all animals. They cannot make their own food, so they eat other living things.
